hs-curricula-saturated-no-standalone: Section II, p.1: the paper says it does not propose quantum computing as a standalone subject because curricula are saturated; the Introduction (p.1) says the same. It is the paper's own scope.
hs-open-source-definition: Section IV, p.4: 'We refer to open source as the collection of freely accessible tools, content, and platforms...' is the paper's own working definition for this paper.
hs-systematic-verification-needed: Section IV-D, p.5: after saying the Section IV-A materials came from domain experts through peer-reviewed channels, the paper says 'Still, there remains a need for a more systematic approach to content verification.' It is a caveat the paper states on the open-resource route it recommends. Its result_type claim is correct as it stands.
hs-modular-scope: Introduction, p.1: 'Rather than proposing a standalone quantum computing course, we suggest a modular approach'. The Conclusion (p.6) repeats the modular approach. Matches the stored value.
slr-method-kitchenham: Section 2, p.2: 'the methodology proposed by Kitchenham et al. [23] is used, thus organizing it into planning, conducting, and reporting the study.' The abstract (p.1) says the same.
slr-period-rationale: Section 2.4, p.5: the period was chosen 'because it corresponds to the beginning of the rise and growth of quantum devices, as well as the proliferation and possible use of noisy quantum computers or NISQ devices.' The reason is stated once and is the paper's own choice. The end year of the period is inconsistent in the paper (2022 versus 2023) but the value does not state it.
slr-research-questions: Section 2.2, pp.3 and 5: RQ1 to RQ4 are listed on p.3 and 'RQ5: Are the experiments carried out on simulators or real quantum devices?' opens p.5, read in context before the PICOC scope list. The value matches all five.
slr-inclusion-criteria: Section 2.3, p.5: IC1 (applied in software or can be simulated or implemented on simulators or quantum devices), IC2 (journal, book, preprint or conference), IC3 (English or Spanish), IC4 (practical solution). Read in full; the value matches all four.
slr-quality-threshold: Section 2.5, p.6: four quality criteria QC1 to QC4, one point each, and 'a score >= 3.0 out of 4.0 points to be selected'. Stated once, not contradicted elsewhere.
slr-ibm-index-included: Section 2.1, p.3: 'We include this not-indexed database with ensured contrasted quality content because essential articles are not included in the other databases.' The paper's own scope choice. The conclusion (p.31) repeats it.
qml-slr-validity-single-reviewer: p.31, the closing validity paragraph of Section 5 (the item anchors it to Section 4): 'to reduce the bias triggered by the number of researchers involved in selecting papers, the first author was the primary reviewer. The other two authors validated the steps of the process.' The paper's own review procedure, stated once and not contradicted.
gb-scope-numerical: Section I, pp.1-2: 'We will numerically analyze the role of squeezing... in both linear and nonlinear tasks. An analytical argument is made to justify such an improvement.' The paper's own method and scope. The quote spans the page break and matches.
gb-platform-loop-squeezed-input: Section II B, p.2: N-mode optical pulse in a closed loop or cavity; input encoded in the squeezing phases of squeezed-vacuum input pulses, one value per pulse.
gb-hamiltonian-active-passive: Section II B, p.3, after Eq. (5): all beta_ij = 0 is called passive, any beta_ij nonzero is active. The Hamiltonian is quadratic in the field operators.
gb-readout-scales-quadratic: Section II B, p.3: 'the readout size scales quadratically with the number of modes N', against the usual linear scaling in optical reservoir computing. Stated for this platform's observable set (N(3N+1)/2 observables).
gb-observables-homodyne-moments: Section II B, p.3: homodyne measurement of the x-quadrature of every mode; only even-order moments are used for squeezed vacuum; the chosen set is second and fourth-order moments.
gb-noise-model-additive-gaussian: Section III, pp.3-4: Eq. (6) additive normally distributed noise of variance sigma_noise^2; p.4: vacuum variance is 1/2, so 0.1 equals 20 percent of vacuum fluctuations.
gb-sim-setup-input-squeezing: Section III, p.4: crystal Hamiltonians generated randomly with every supermode squeezed by e^-r; input pulses squeezed with fixed r_input = 2 (about 8.7 dB). Appendix A (p.8) gives the matching construction.
gb-three-tasks: Section III, p.4: three tasks (linear memory, NARMA, Mackey-Glass forecasting); performance checked on an additional test input sequence, mainly by the mean-square error of Eq. (4).
gb-linear-memory-setup: Section III A, p.4: C(d) = 1 - min MSE(y, y(d)) is defined and training and test sets of 4000 and 1000 inputs are stated.
gb-delay-cut-definition: Section III A, p.4 and Figure 2 caption: 'the delay at which the linear capacity drops below 0.9 (which we also call the delay cut)'.
gb-narma-setup: Section III B, p.5: NARMA10 with default constants (0.3, 0.05, 1.5, 0.1) and the stated requirement of high linear capacity up to delay 10 plus low error on s(k-1)s(k-10).
gb-mackey-glass-setup: Section III C, p.6: tau = 17 chaotic, sampled at time resolution 3, target is the next value, encoding phi = pi s, and the autonomous driving protocol.
gm-def-dla: Definition 1, Section II B, p.3: stated verbatim, with Eq. (5) g = span_R <iG>_Lie.
gm-def-overparametrization: Definition 2, Section II B, p.4: the paper's own definition, with Eq. (8).
gm-def-unital-pauli: Definition 3, Section II C, p.5, and the assumption c in (-1, 1) 'necessary for Lemma 2 in Appendix E to hold, i.e., for the identity operator to be the only fixed point'. Both are the paper's own definition and assumption.
gm-setup-qnn-model: Section II A, p.2 (Eqs. 1 to 3: U = product of exp(-i theta_m H_m), H_m traceless Hermitian from a generator set G) and Section II C, p.5 (noise channels N_m before and after each unitary, Eq. 18).
gm-theorem1-end-noise-rank: Theorem 1, Section III B, p.10: a single noise channel at the end of the QNN cannot raise the rank of the QFIM. Appendix A, p.17 proves it from the QFIM property 'non-increasing under quantum channels' (listed on p.6 as property 5) by a null-space argument on F(noiseless) - F(noisy) >= 0. That property is a standard fact, not a specific paper's theorem. The statement carries its condition (one channel at the end).
gm-theorem3-global-depol-suppression: Theorem 3, Section III B, p.10: stated for global depolarizing channels before and after every unitary. Appendix C, p.18 proves it: by convexity and F(identity/d) = 0, F(noisy) <= (1-p)^(M+1) F(noiseless), so every eigenvalue is at most (1-p)^(M+1) lambda_max(noiseless) <= e^(-p(M+1)) lambda_max; the entries follow from Eq. C6. The constant in O is the noiseless QFIM, independent of p. Uses convexity of the QFIM and 1-p <= e^-p only. Convexity is one of the QFIM properties the paper lists on p.6 and defers to [61] for their proof ('we refer the reader to [61] for their proof'); I treat it as a standard property, as for Theorem 1's monotonicity, and the coordinator may reverse both.
gm-toy-model-setup: Section III A, pp.6-7: single qubit, state rho = 0.9|+><+| + 0.1 I/2 (Eq. 24), four rotations Z, X, Z, X (Eq. 25), bit-flip noise; 'We choose a full rank state to avoid issues in the QFIM (namely, discontinuities in its entries)'.
gm-num-setup-hva: Section IV, p.11: double precision, qibo with the qibojit backend on CPUs (Intel Core i7-9750H and AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3955WX), Hamiltonian variational ansatz with transverse-field Ising generators and periodic boundary conditions (Eqs. 39 and 40).
gm-limit-capacity-modification-future: Section V, p.13: the paper proposes the modified measure D1^(epsilon) (Eq. 42) and says 'We leave however the study of such a measure for future work'. It states what it does not cover.
gm-limit-no-average-rank-proof: Section III C, p.10: 'we will not attempt to prove that, on average, noise increases the rank of the QFIM', because there are special noise types and parameters where the rank is not raised (Sections III A and III B), and 'we will leave a more detailed rank analysis for future work'. The paper states the limit itself. Its true result type is a stated limit, not a claim.
gm-limit-noise-before-first-gate: Section III B, p.9: the noise channel acts before the first parametrized gate 'we avoid the change of rank in the quantum state (from a pure state to a full-rank state) that would occur otherwise'. A choice of noise model the paper states; Section III C (p.10) repeats it for N_1.
gm-limit-quasi-regime-future-work: Section VI, p.14: 'We leave for future work to study the performance and potential for quantum advantage of parametrized quantum circuits in this quasi-overparametrized regime.' A scope limit the paper states.
some-noise-cannot-raise-rank: Theorem 1 (p.10; proved in Appendix A, p.17) and Theorem 2 (p.10; proved in Appendix B, p.17-18 by pulling the global depolarizing channels to the end through Eqs. 29 and 30 and applying Theorem 1). Both are stated with their conditions. The new value is narrower and more exact than the stored one: the stored sentence also names 'measurement noise', which the paper only states as a consequence in the conclusion (p.13) and does not prove separately. Theorem 2 uses the commutation of depolarizing channels, a standard step shown by the equations.
gp-def-gaussian-process: Definition 1, Section I, p.2: a GP is a collection whose every finite subvector is multivariate Gaussian; 'Said otherwise, every linear combination ... follows a univariate Gaussian distribution.' Both halves of the value are in the passage.
gp-setup-observables: Section II, p.2: dataset states with purity in Omega(1/poly(log d)), observables from a set O with Tr[O_j O_j'] = d delta and O_j^2 = identity (Pauli strings), outputs C_j(rho_i) = Tr[U rho_i U^dagger O_j] (Eq. 1).
gp-lemma1-zero-mean-uncorrelated-observa: Lemma 1, Section II A, p.3 is stated for both U(d) and O(d). Supp. Info. E (pp.44-45) proves it exactly (not only at large d) from the k = 1 and k = 2 twirl formulas, Eqs. (C6) and (C11) for U(d), with the orthogonal case from Eqs. (D7) and (D12). The covariance for j different from j' is zero; the j = j' formulas are given.
gp-theorem1-positive-correlation: Theorem 1, Section II B, p.4 and Supp. Info. H, p.47: stated under the same conditions as Lemma 2 (large d, overlaps in Omega(1/poly(log d))). The proof matches Lemma 2's moments with Isserlis' theorem (Eq. H1) and gets uniqueness from Carleman's condition and the result in [37] that determinate marginals give a determinate joint law. Those are standard moment-problem tools, not a specific paper's theorem. Covariance is Tr[rho_i rho_i']/d for U(d) and twice that for O(d), as in the value. It rests on Lemma 2 (graded LOW only because of the value's omission).
gp-proof-strategy-moments: Section I, p.1: 'Hence, our proof strategy boils down to showing that each moment of the QNN's output distribution converges to that of a multivariate Gaussian', after saying the entries of unitary matrices are not independent. Methods IV A (p.7) repeats that one cannot rely on the central limit theorem. This is the paper's own method, stated once.
gp-twirl-asymptotic-formula: Lemma 3 (main text, p.8) and Supplemental Theorem 1 (Supp. Info. C, p.19): the proof builds the Gram matrix A = d^k (A0 + B/d) with A0 its own inverse (Supplemental Proposition 5, p.22), inverts it by the matrix identity of Supplemental Lemma 1 (a textbook identity, cited to [51]) and bounds the correction entries by O(1/d) (p.23). The paper cites [50, 52] for the Gram matrix being invertible (linear independence of the permutation operators for d >= k, the Schur-Weyl commutant) and does not prove it; I treat that as a textbook tool under F129, and the coordinator may reverse. The formula is for fixed k and large d. Pages 20-21 and 25-26 (Propositions 2 to 4 and 7 to 9) and the orthogonal pages 34-42 take no cited result as a step; only [50], [50, 52] and [51] appear in this chain, and [53] appears first in Supplemental Theorem 4.
gp-supp-prop6-trace-even-cycles: Supplemental Proposition 6, Supp. Info. C 2, p.24: proved in full by the cycle decomposition of sigma (Eq. C35) and O^2 = identity: an odd cycle gives Tr[O] = 0, and r even cycles give d^r. The statement carries its conditions (O traceless, Hermitian, unitary; sigma a product of r disjoint cycles of even length).
gp-open-other-architectures: Section III, p.7: 'Finally, we leave for future work the study of whether GPs arise in other architectures, such as matchgate circuits [46, 47].' The paper states what it does not cover.
qnn-gp-convergence-proof: Section III, p.7 states the headline 'under certain conditions' and Theorem 1 (Section II B, p.4; Supp. Info. H, p.47) proves it for the positively correlated case, for both U(d) and O(d), by moment matching (Lemma 2, Supp. Info. C to F) plus Isserlis and the moment-problem result [37]. The 'certain conditions' wording is met by Theorem 1. Theorems 2 and 3 are graded LOW separately (Theorem 2: main text and SI differ and the proof is three lines; Theorem 3: relies on the Weingarten asymptotics of [53]). If the team lead reads this stored claim as covering all three theorems, it would be LOW for that reason.
qnn-gp-haar-scope: Introduction, p.1: 'Our results are derived for QNNs that are Haar random over the unitary and orthogonal groups.' Verbatim.
qnn-gp-not-all-qnns: Section III, p.7: 'Haar random QNNs will not necessarily always converge to a GP. That is, not all QNNs and all measurements will lead to a GP.' A caveat the paper states about its own result.

theory_low.gb-theory-spectral-norm-bound: Appendix B 2, p.8 gives ||A^d|| = R^(d/2) ||S^d||, the passive equality (||S^d|| = ||S|| = 1, with 'trivial to show' that powers of a passive S are passive), and then simply states ||A^d|| >= R^(d/2) for the active case. The lower bound needs ||S^d|| >= 1 for a symplectic S, and the paper gives no argument for it. Section IV (p.6) says 'It can be analytically shown'. The memory-retention reading is the authors' modelling choice. Not a proved result as written.
theory_low.gb-theory-passive-iff-unit-singular: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix A, p.8 takes the Bloch-Messiah decomposition from refs [70, 71] and then says 'So the transformation is passive iff all the singular values of S are equal to 1'. The link between beta_ij = 0 (the passive definition) and an orthogonal S is not derived in the paper, and neither direction is proved.
theory_low.gm-theorem4-general-pauli-suppression: Theorem 4, Section III C, p.11 is stated with its noise model, but the Appendix D proof (pp.18-19) rests on Lemma 1, whose proof (Appendix E, p.19) takes Lemma 2 'Mueller-Hermes/Franca/Wolf [83], Theorem 6.1' (relative entropy of a local depolarized state contracts by (1-p)^2) as a step. A proof that uses another paper's theorem is not a proved result here. Also the closing lines of Appendix D (p.19) print 'O(pM+1)' in one place and O((1-p)^(2(M+1))) in the next, a typo in the text layer or the paper.
theory_low.gm-theorem5-qubit-dependent: Theorem 5, Appendix F, pp.19-20: the proof reduces to Theorem 4 ('From here one can follow the proof of Theorem 4'), which rests on the cited Theorem 6.1 of Mueller-Hermes, Franca and Wolf [83]. The printed bound O(q^(2(M+1))) also disagrees with what the proof gives: Appendix D closes with (1-p)^(2(M+1)), so with q it should be (1-q)^(2(M+1)) <= e^(-2q(M+1)). As printed, q^(2(M+1)) is a typo and the value repeats it.
theory_low.gm-lemma1-relative-entropy: Lemma 1, Appendix D, p.19: its proof (Appendix E, p.19) is a short combination of Lemma 2, which is the cited result of Mueller-Hermes, Franca and Wolf [83] (Theorem 6.1, rephrased), and monotonicity of relative entropy under the unital Pauli channel. The key (1-p)^2 contraction is the cited theorem, not proved in this paper.
theory_low.gm-lemma3-reversed-order: Lemma 3, Appendix F, p.20: the statement is quoted, but the proof is only 'follows that of Lemma 1', which rests on the cited [83] Theorem 6.1. No proof is given for the reversed order.
theory_low.gm-global-depol-commutes-to-end: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section III B, p.9 says 'It is not hard to see' that global depolarizing channels commute through unitary channels, then writes Eqs. (29) to (31). No argument is given for the commutation step. The identity is standard but it is stated, not proved.
theory_low.gm-toy-noiseless-ranks: Section III A, p.7: a computed result for one toy model at three parameter sets (rank 1, 2, 2). A short reason is given only for theta_1. It is a one-example computation, not a general statement.
theory_low.gm-toy-noisy-rank-increase: Section III A, p.8: a computed result for one toy model at three parameter sets with bit-flip p = 0.1; the rank goes from two to three only at theta_3. A measured or computed example, not a proof. The 'noise channels effectively applied at the end' reading is tied to Theorem 1.
theory_low.gm-new-direction-preserves-purity: Section III A, pp.8-9: a result read from trajectories in Figure 5(b) for one toy model at one parameter set. The paper itself notes this does not mean the QNN purifies the state.
theory_low.gm-noise-induced-barren-plateau: Section III B, p.10: Eq. (36) is shown only for a linear loss under global depolarizing noise, and the link to 'noise-induced barren plateau' is the authors' reading. The wider claim that insensitivities arise already at state space level is an interpretation.
theory_low.gm-purity-altering-directions: Section VI, p.14 summarizes a finding from the single-qubit example (Figures 5 and 6, pp.8-9). It is a result from one toy model, stated as general in the conclusion.
theory_low.gm-noise-raises-rank-capacity-d1-d2: Section V, p.13: the D1 statement follows from the rank result, and the D2 statement uses the cited inequalities [68] and [69] (Eq. 41 and rank F >= rank I). The point rests on the paper's own rank results, which are shown by example and simulation, and on cited inequalities. An implication, not a theorem.
theory_low.gm-full-rank-but-insensitive: Section V, pp.13-14: 'one can expect that in the regime where the noise is sufficiently large' the QFIM is full rank with exponentially small eigenvalues. It combines the simulated rank increase with Theorem 4 (graded LOW here). An author conclusion, not a proved statement.
theory_low.capacity-measures-ill-defined: The new value is more exact than the stored one: it names the measures (Refs. [27, 28]) and the reason (rank counts non-zero eigenvalues, not their size), as Section V (p.13) and Section VI (p.14) say. It is the authors' conclusion from their rank and eigenvalue results and from Theorem 4 (graded LOW here); the paper does not test any modified measure. 'Ill-defined' is the abstract's word, and Section VI says 'can be misleading'. An author interpretation, so LOW.
theory_low.noise-suppresses-qfim-eigenvalues: The new value is narrower and right: only the two noise models of Theorem 3 (global depolarizing, proved in Appendix C) and Theorem 4 (local depolarizing plus unital Pauli, Appendix D). The stored value says 'as the magnitude of noise increases all the eigenvalues... become exponentially suppressed' with no model, which the paper proves only for those two. Graded by the weaker half: Theorem 4's proof uses the cited Theorem 6.1 of Mueller-Hermes, Franca and Wolf [83] (via Lemma 1 and Lemma 2), so the value is LOW. Theorem 3 alone is HIGH (see gm-theorem3-global-depol-suppression).; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.gp-lemma2-moments-pairings: Lemma 2, Section II A, p.3 and Supp. Info. F, p.45. The quote carries only the odd-moment half. The value's even-moment formula (d^(-k/2) times the sum over pairings of the overlap products) holds for U(d) only; for O(d) the lemma carries an extra factor 2^(k/2) (printed '= E_O[...], 2^(k/2)' in Eq. 6, and Eq. G6 gives k!/(d^(k/2) (k/2)!) against k!/(d^(k/2) 2^(k/2) (k/2)!) for U(d)). The value states one formula for 'a Haar random QNN' and drops that factor. The proof in Supp. Info. F is one sentence pointing to Eqs. (C52) and (D60). Also, the large-d condition and the purity condition are not in the quote.
theory_low.gp-theorem2-uncorrelated: Theorem 2, Section II C, p.4 and Supp. Info. I, p.47. The main text gives diagonal entries Tr[rho_i^2]/d (Eq. 7), but the SI restatement (Eq. I1) and its proof print 1/d. The proof is three lines: it compares Isserlis' formula with Eqs. (C55) and (D61) and says 'it is clear'. It uses Supplemental Theorem 3 (p.27) only by a passing reference. The conditions are split between the statement and the dataset assumptions (overlap exactly 1/d and purity in Omega(1/poly(log(1/d)))) and the text layer cuts the quote. Not settled as stated.
theory_low.gp-theorem3-negative-correlation: Theorem 3, Section II D, pp.4-5 and Supp. Info. J, pp.47-48. The covariances are exact from Lemma 1 (-1/(d^2-1) is about -1/d^2). But the higher moments are matched using Supplemental Theorems 4 and 5, whose proofs (Supp. Info. C 4, pp.29-30) take the large-d asymptotics of the Weingarten functions from [53] (Collins 2003) as a step. That is a cited result, so the statement is not settled by this paper alone.
theory_low.gp-corollary1-univariate-variance: Corollary 1, Section II E, p.5 and Supp. Info. G, p.46: the statement says P(C_j(rho_i)) = N(0, sigma^2) with sigma^2 = 1/d or 2/d, with no large-d condition. The proof uses Lemma 2, which is a large-d result, so what is proved is the limit. At finite d the variance is not 1/d (Lemma 1 gives 1/(d+1) for a pure state under U(d)), and C_j is bounded in [-1, 1], so it cannot be exactly Gaussian. The value drops the 'large-d limit' and the purity condition.
theory_low.gp-corollary2-tail-bound: Corollary 2, Section II G, pp.6-7 and Supp. Info. L, p.50. The proof (Eqs. L1 to L5) treats C_j as exactly N(0, 1/d) and reads the tail probability off the Gaussian. Convergence of moments, or of the law, in the large-d limit does not by itself give a tail bound at fixed c. The main text introduces the corollary only for U Haar over U(d), and the statement and the value drop that. The step to the gradient uses the parameter-shift rule and a union bound with the same Gaussian assumption.
theory_low.gp-doubly-exponential-concentration: Section II G, p.7: the doubly exponential vanishing follows from Corollary 2 (graded LOW) by d = 2^n. The comparisons with Chebyshev's inequality and with Levy's lemma [28] are stated, not derived, in the main text.
theory_low.gp-abstract-concentration-worse: Abstract, p.1 and Section II G, p.6: an interpretation of Corollaries 1 and 2 ('worse than previously thought'; deep orthogonal QNNs will exhibit barren plateaus, 'a result not previously known'). A claim of novelty and an interpretation, resting on Corollary 2.
theory_low.gp-corollary3-t-designs: Corollary 3, Section II H, p.7 and Supp. Info. M, p.50: the proof is two lines. It appeals to Theorems 1, 2 and 3 and to a t-design matching the first t Haar moments. The claim is stated 'under the same conditions for which Theorems 1, 2 and 3 hold', so it inherits Theorem 2's unsettled statement and Theorem 3's reliance on the cited Weingarten asymptotics [53].
theory_low.gp-theorem4-generalized-datasets: Methods IV B, p.9 (main text Theorem 4) and Supp. Info. N, p.51 (stated as Theorem 5 there). The numbering swap is correctly noted in the anchor and value. The SI proof is one paragraph: 'simply follows that of Theorems 1 and 2' with each overlap condition replaced by its average, 'the rest of the proofs are the same'. Replacing a pointwise bound by an average is not shown to pass through the moment bounds. It also inherits Theorem 2's unsettled statement.
theory_low.gp-practical-cases-generalized: Methods IV B, pp.9-10: the multiclass well-separated case is 'it can be verified'; only the Haar-random-states case is computed (Eq. 24, expected overlap 1/d). The value says the condition 'arises precisely when' the states are Haar random, but the computation shows only that Haar random states satisfy it, not the converse.
theory_low.gp-theorem5-noisy-prediction-trivial: Theorem 5 in the main text (Methods IV C, p.11), Theorem 4 in Supp. Info. K (pp.48-49): the numbering swap is correctly noted. The conditions are dropped from the statement and value: the shot noise is modelled as Gaussian with variance 1/N, the result is for the large-d limit, and the proof treats the number of training states m as fixed (the O(N/d) and O(N/d^2) bounds on m^T C and m^T m ignore that these sums have m terms). The value carries none of these conditions.
theory_low.gp-predictive-power-exponential-measurem: Section II F, p.6: the exponential measurement requirement follows from the covariance suppression (Lemma 1) and the Gaussian shot-noise model of the Methods; the polynomial case for n' in O(log n) is argued in the Methods. An author conclusion on a model, not a theorem.
theory_low.gp-kernel-connection: Section II B, p.4: the authors recognize the kernel as proportional to the fidelity kernel. It is an interpretation of Theorem 1 with citations [38 to 40].
theory_low.gp-supp-theorem4-orthogonal-moments: Supplemental Theorem 4, Supp. Info. C 4, pp.29-30: the proof of Supplemental Proposition 10 begins 'Let us start by using known results for the asymptotics of the Weingarten functions [53]' (Collins 2003) and takes c_(e,pi)/d^k = mu(pi)/d^(k+|pi|_t) from it. That is a specific cited result used as the key step.
theory_low.gp-supp-theorem5-repeated-orthogonal: Supplemental Theorem 5, Supp. Info. C 4, pp.30-31: the second-sum terms use 'known results for the asymptotics of the Weingarten functions [53]', as in Supplemental Theorem 4. A cited result used as a step, so not a proved result here.
theory_low.gp-supp-theorem9-orthogonal-group-orthog: Supplemental Theorem 9, Supp. Info. D 4, p.43 (proof on p.44): the paper says the proof 'follows similarly to that of Supplemental Theorem 4' with an extra factor 2^(k/2). No proof is written out, and Supplemental Theorem 4 relies on the cited Weingarten asymptotics [53].
